documents.title: The artist's guide
documents.description: Your complete workflow, from the first surface to the final refinement.
documents.html:
Start with a layer#

Create a Cyrus Scatter controller, add a layer, assign its receiving surfaces and add models or Points. Set Amount, then press Update scatter in Manual mode. Live responds to relevant edits.

Use Geometry > Cyrus > Cyrus Scatter to create a controller, then exit Create mode and select it in Modify. Each layer owns its surfaces, sources, amount, layout, transforms and spacing. Layer order matters when between-layer spacing is enabled.

Use Add, Copy, Remove, Up and Down to organize layers. Copy includes independent Paint Areas. Visible controls viewport display; Enabled controls the layer contribution. Removing an assignment does not delete the source scene object.

In 0.82.6, closed sections create controls on first opening and reuse them while the command panel remains mounted. Switching layers rebinds those controls. Browsing does not apply pending Manual edits.

Schema 61 stores reviewed plant preparation, physical minimum distances and source-bound colliders. Schema-60 preparation needs explicit review or repair. Schema-59 scenes open with Interactions off. Schema-58 scenes require the explicit Undoable Upgrade scene action. Preserve original files and save upgraded copies.

Scene source access#

In Models & Points, highlight source rows and expand Source access. Select sources selects their scene nodes. Show sources and Hide sources change node visibility in one Undo while preserving renderable flags, registration, materials and completed plants. Max layer/group/category visibility restrictions still apply.

For one model with an assigned material, Edit material opens that scene material in Slate. Shared instances change together. Point/Empty, mixed and missing-material selections are guarded; library asset files remain unchanged.

Surfaces, models and optional containers#

Add receivers to the selected layer. Unchanged receivers retain their base random streams when another receiver is added, renamed or reordered. Density gives each receiver its own count below the cap; Fixed Total redistributes the same total, so some existing candidates may be removed. Geometry changes, Relax, masks and shared spacing can change accepted output.

Use + below Models & Points to add a model. Add Point, beside Make point, creates markers without final model geometry. Pick object replaces one selected Point or existing model while preserving its row identity, label, weight, scale, radius, offset and Band assignments. Make point converts a model row to a Point; the original scene object is retained. Duplicate sources and receiver picks are rejected. Empty choices create weighted gaps in Candidate budget mode; Accepted target rejects positive-weight Empty rows.

Source controls include label, identification color, weight, scale, Manual/Auto radius, vertical offset and forward axis. Manual preserves its radius and optional Follow Scale. Auto bounds supported geometry around the pivot after final instance scale and orientation; it is conservative spacing, not exact mesh collision. Points, Empty and unqualified source families remain Manual. Assignment-group colors are separate from identification colors.

Source containers are optional palettes. New rectangles start with Enable collection off. Position and resize first, then enable collection to collect eligible source pivots. Selecting a rectangle opens compact collection and dimension controls; select the Scatter controller for full planting settings. Moving an enabled rectangle carries its owned models; resizing its boundary leaves their transforms unchanged. Disabling collection parks models while retaining settings. Manual waits for Update; Live applies relevant membership changes.

Removing the last model clears its scattered output after Update in Manual, or automatically in Live. The empty layer remains valid when Amount changes. Adding a replacement restores planting. Point and intentional Empty gap rows retain their distinct behavior.

Layout and Amount#

Planting positions chooses Surface random, Rectangular, Staggered or Hexagonal. Grids expose world-unit spacing, fixed Origin X/Y, Heading and stable Jitter. They project down onto the highest receiver hit. Hexagonal calculates row pitch from its nearest-neighbor distance. Count/Density and refill are inactive; masks and collision rules thin the lattice. Source assignment below is independent. Entirely vertical receivers and Analyzer Single/EdgeRow positions are unsupported with grids.

Random mix chooses weighted sources. Clusters choose assignment groups across space. Spline Bands use closed world-XY Paths, explicit Models / Points or Assignment groups, and Consecutive or Independent ranges. Surface Analyzer consumes separately analyzed boundary, path and point channels.

Consecutive accumulates widths separately on each Path/side and preserves unassigned intervals as gaps. Independent exposes each Band's Start/End and combines eligible contributions. New Bands start unassigned. Scaling a Path changes its outline, not its world-space Band distances.

Density and its optional curve shape a Band's contribution from Start to End. Independent contributions cap total occupancy at 100%, then choose the Band proportionally. A 100% Sphere plus 25% Box gives approximately 80% Sphere/20% Box in the overlap and 25% occupancy where only Box contributes, before other masks/spacing.

Rounded uses distance to original border segments. Sharp uses bounded miter offsets; acute corners have limits and narrow/complex requests can require simplification. The preview shows admitted geometry.

Amount supports Count or area Density, up to 1,000,000 per population. A controller shares a 1,000,000-candidate work limit across its populations, including retry and protected-edit requirements. Exceeding that limit reports an error and retains the preceding result. Candidate budget can underfill after restrictions. Independent ranges and nontrivial Band density require Candidate budget; Accepted target is rejected so retries cannot erase the fade. Use a fixed seed for repeatable comparisons. Texture Density uses a selected UV channel (1..99, default 1) on each receiver. Choose 64, 128, 256 or 512 samples per side (default 128). Higher resolution helps capture narrow mask details at a greater preparation cost. UVs clamp to 0..1; white permits and black excludes. Unchanged maps reuse their sampled data across receiver edits. Errors identify the invalid receiver/channel and retain the previous complete result.

0.86.0 keeps placement-sized calculation and storage in native memory. Count changes no longer reserve MAXScript heap proportional to every plant. Undo remains available; a failed successor preserves the last complete result. The one-million controller work limit and memory safeguards remain. Large calculations, complex source geometry and Bake can still block Max while they finish.

Image, map and surface density#

Image / pattern density and Surface density are independent. White permits plants, black excludes them and gray thins them. Their enabled fields multiply with Paint and terrain eligibility before spacing.

Choose pattern selects Uniform, Soft patches or Wide bands. Image selects a file. Both choose projected World XY. Physical tile size, rotation, offsets and Repeat/Clamp control the image footprint. Scatter local XY follows the setup frame; Receiver UV reads the explicitly selected UV channel.

Map selects Map coordinates and evaluates supported graphs against each receiver. Vertex Color reads its own numeric channel, and Checker reads its own UV channel. Color Correction and Output chains retain those inputs. Supported classes also include Bitmap, Mix, Noise, RGB Multiply and Gradient. A surface material is not a density map; renderer/camera-dependent graphs reject with a useful explanation.

Both Map targets accept a TextureMap dragged from the Material Editor, including when empty. Procedural maps show a small cached thumbnail. Drag the texture map itself rather than a complete material. Receiver-dependent graphs can look different on the surface; use Show mask to inspect their evaluated density.

Clear removes the map and disables image density. The independent surface field stays enabled if it was enabled. Disabling Use image alone preserves its map for later. Image or pattern selection restores projected coordinates; Map restores receiver-aware coordinates.

Enable Use surface density and choose Mesh channel to read stored numeric values from the evaluated receiver. Channel 0 reads vertex colors; channels 1..99 select numbered map data. Choose R/X, G/Y or B/Z, then Input min/max, Invert and the response curve. Every receiver must contain the requested channel. Data Channel or VertexPaint can author it; Scatter does not invent missing data.

Relative elevation uses evaluated local height: low is 0, high is 1 and flat terrain is 0. Node translation, rotation and scale preserve this field. It creates no mesh channel. Valley moss and Mountain planting use it so their library entries no longer depend on channel 2 or the original world altitude.

Show mask displays Image, Surface field or Combined density and follows relevant edits. Manual plants remain at the last Update while the preview can show current inputs. Live follows relevant map/channel edits and animation. Idle and unrelated animation do not evaluate maps or solve Scatter. A failed update retains the complete previous result.

Native map sampling uses unfiltered scalar values. The map graph and receiver work are bounded; unsupported requirements and oversized inputs reject cleanly. Projected maps can use an explicit portable image snapshot. Receiver-aware graphs remain editable in Max scenes but cannot be exported as arbitrary procedural packages or baked into a context-free tile.

Band scale profiles#

In Layout, Scale sits directly below the density curve. Min/Max supplies random size variation. Scale profile selects Off, Follow Density or Custom. Custom enables Edit scale curve. X runs from Band Start to End; Y is size percent, where 100% preserves size.

Density and scale have independent curves. Follow Density uses the effective density curve shape, without the Density % strength; disabling that density curve gives a flat 100% scale profile. Switching modes keeps the Custom graph. Zero size does not remove a candidate.

Scale curves multiply existing source, Band and layer size once. Auto Radius follows final size; Manual radius needs Follow Scale. Size-dependent spacing can change accepted counts. Manual requires Update scatter. Steep Sharp profiles can exceed the bounded precision and retain the previous result; simplify the curve or choose Rounded.

Slope and altitude filters#

Enable Filter slope or Filter altitude in Include / exclude areas > Surface eligibility. Slope is measured from world up using the evaluated geometric normal: 0 degrees upward, 90 degrees vertical, 180 degrees downward. Altitude is world Z at the final receiver anchor, before source pivot offsets.

Lower and Upper fade soften density inside the range. For a 0-35 degree slope interval, a 10 degree upper fade thins between 25 and 35 degrees. Zero fade includes the endpoint. Fades cannot overlap; invalid settings retain the previous complete result.

Filters preserve surviving candidate IDs, model choices and transforms. Paint overlap still uses max-union density; explicitly moved or cloned CS Edit plants bypass these filters. Spacing and cleanup follow filtering. Use Candidate budget to retain the visible density fade; Accepted target can refill within its finite work budget.

Manual waits for Update; Live follows relevant edits and receiver animation. The status describes the last calculated prepared pool, separately from accepted plants. Heights use scene units and survive scene-unit conversion.

Named settings and curve presets#

Use Presets... in Amount, Transforms or Spacing & cleanup. Curve presets are available from Paint, Analyzer and Band density/scale graphs. Save new captures a named item; selecting it is passive, and Apply changes the target shown in the dialog. Reopen the browser to target a different layer.

Population includes amount, density, seed and retry policy. Transforms include the layer rotation, scale, movement, normal alignment and projection. Assets, surfaces, IDs, maps and layout remain linked to the scene. Physical distances convert across system units; density stays per square metre.

Spacing stores the effective rule and applies an explicit override in the chosen Within this layer or Between layers scope. It does not store peer identities or change Relax/cleanup. Reset inheritance remains a separate control.

Curve presets preserve samples and editable handles while retaining enable flags, widths and scale ranges. Density and Paint scale use zero-to-one values; other scale curves support multipliers. Invalid or incompatible curves are rejected. One Undo/Redo restores Apply, and closing a graph after Undo does not reapply the preset.

Manual waits for Update scatter; Live follows normal update callbacks. Browsing, saving and renaming do not calculate plants. Animated or expression-controlled targets are rejected. Static shared controllers are detached so another owner is preserved.

The local library is CyrusScatter/Presets inside the per-user Max PlugCFG directory. Share the .cspreset.json files. Limits are 512 files, 64 KiB per file and 80-character names. Rename changes the library name; Delete confirms removal of the selected file. Invalid files and failed writes report errors. Complete static recipes and explicit role substitution are available through Layers > Recipes.

Vector painting#

Turn on Use Paint Areas, add a named area and choose one receiver from the layer. Select Paint or Erase, set Radius and press Start Brush. Paint joins circular footprints into a vector region; Erase cuts coverage and holes. Stop ends the session.

Areas share the layer models and population. Overlap contributes coverage once per candidate. Turning Paint Areas off retains the areas and uses the full receiver. Fill and Clear operate on the selected area; keep a saved copy before major edits.

Inward/outward feather widths and separate density/scale curves shape the edge. Density changes acceptance; scale multiplies model size. A 100 mm radius has a 200 mm diameter. Borders describe coverage, not guaranteed accepted plants.

Hover over Paint controls for short descriptions. Fade density changes plant acceptance; Fade scale changes size independently. Inside and Outside fade define the transition width. With the default curve, Edge scale is the outer-end size multiplier and Inner scale is the interior multiplier: 0.5 means half size, 1 unchanged and 2 double. Edge scale cannot exceed Inner scale. The graph shapes the transition between them.

Vector painting supports terrain, spheres, boxes, vertical sides and manifold curved meshes. Curved strokes follow surface distance across connected edges without painting through to the opposite side or disconnected sheets. Degenerate faces and nonmanifold connections require repair.

The vector format introduced in 0.78 does not convert earlier stroke setups. Preserve older scenes with their matching build and create a new setup for the vector workflow.

Curved Paint retains Paint/Erase, Fill/Clear, independent density and scale fade curves, Undo/Redo and saved scenes. Curved mesh distance includes nonuniform receiver scaling. Surface coverage uses vector face regions with bounded work: up to 100,000 triangles and 200,000 vertices, with separate contour and solver limits. Terrain keeps its existing projected vector behavior.

Paint and spline snapshots#

Stop the brush and select a Paint Area. Export spline offers Optimized and Exact snapshot. Optimized reduces planar knots within a world-unit maximum deviation, initially 1 mm, and reports the reduction; attached-surface boundaries default to Exact. Cases that cannot be certified retain Exact geometry with a reason. Export leaves original Paint and completed plants unchanged. Reopen the options if the captured owner, area or receiver changes. Edit the exported spline, then choose Replace or Add and Pick spline... to import it explicitly.

For terrain, export uses the receiver's local XY plane at local Z=0 with its scene transform. On terrain the spline is a planar editing guide. Import projects along receiver-local Z, clips to the receiver and requires every contour to be closed. Nested loops and self-intersections use even-odd fill regardless of winding or order.

Replace sets coverage; Add unions it with the existing region without erasing paint. Density, fades, models and area identity stay unchanged. A changed import and each export are one Undo. Manual waits for Update; Live follows changed coverage. There is no live source link: later spline edits require another import.

Curve tolerance is a world-unit approximation distance, initially 1 mm. Smaller values need more samples. An edited shape is limited to 8,192 input knots and 8,192 sampled vertices; unchanged guarded surface snapshots use the canonical contour budget. Paint precision imposes a minimum tolerance; very large local coordinates can prevent accurate Max spline export. Invalid conversion retains existing paint. Reopen using the saved scene units; native Paint geometry conversion guards still apply.

Curved receivers export a 3D surface border. An unchanged exported snapshot restores exact coverage, including holes and large regions. Edited closed curves must lie on the receiver within Curve tolerance and select the smaller enclosed region on a closed component. A fully filled closed object has no border to export. The generic 8,192-knot import limit applies to edited curves; exact guarded snapshots use the native contour limit.

Area limits, transforms and spacing#

Closed Include shapes union their eligible domains. Exclude takes precedence. Area masks test placement support rather than trimming model geometry. Layout & soft boundaries explains guide widths and edge curves.

Rotation, XYZ scale, whole scale and movement have independent ranges and reset buttons. Projection and orientation settings affect final placement.

In Models & Points > Radius and clearance, give each selected model its radius and independently choose Own copies, Other models in this layer and Other layers. Each scope can use layer defaults or its own supported request. Other-layer requests can target selected layers or all other layers in this setup.

For an explicit model request, clearance is factor × (radius A + radius B) + gap, measured in XY or full 3D. Protected edits reserve space first, then eligible preferred models, then layer and stable candidate order. Prefer this model resolves conflicts after Count admission; it does not take extra Count slots. These are pivot-radius tests rather than exact mesh collisions.

Use Spacing & cleanup for layer defaults and candidate Relax. Point Relax and Boundary Relax are visible above Advanced. Enabling a mode reveals its controls. The shared Relax distance means desired separation for Point Relax or neighbor-search radius for Boundary Relax; it stays editable when either is enabled. Boundary Relax smooths candidates within its movement cap. Clearance filters the moved candidates afterward.

Advanced retains layer-owned selected-instance radius overrides and accepted cleanup. Cyrus Scatter Edit > Instances adjusts published instances using stable candidate/source identities. Generation and receiver changes can invalidate bindings; a blocked edit retains its saved history. Radius overlays are inspection aids. In Manual mode, press Update scatter to apply placement edits.

Preview, updates, output and diagnostics#

Placement points shows one marker per accepted placement. Point Cloud, Proxy and Mesh have separate display budgets, so shown counts can be lower than accepted output. Choose Textured mesh in Display mode for supported source base colors, UV channels and cutout opacity. Color by offers Layer, Model and Bands identification colors for nontextured modes. Use Surfaces > Hide surface to hide receiver drawing while keeping painting and rendering. The choice is shared by setups using that node and supports Undo and scene saving.

Textured Mesh covers Standard and Corona Legacy/Physical base color and opacity, Multi/Sub face IDs and supported Bitmap, Checker and Color Correction map chains. Each color or opacity branch requires one common explicit UV channel; the branches may differ. The two-sided preview uses bounded 256-pixel tiles and an alpha cutoff, rather than full Corona shading, translucency or blended transparency. Forest Color omits per-instance Forest variation. Unsupported branches report fallback; missing UV channels retain the preceding complete display. Source render materials are preserved.

Supported material, UV and color-management edits refresh appearance without changing placement publication or applying pending Manual edits. Colored Mesh preserves supported leaf cutouts while showing identification colors. Radius-only updates reuse compatible source geometry, UVs and material data. Source geometry changes still require Update before the new appearance can be paired with the plants; shared animated maps follow relevant forward and reverse time changes.

Color by Bands follows the accepted owner even when Bands share a model. Preview Falloff shows selected contribution or Combined density on receiver surfaces: blue is zero and red is 100%. Show Boundaries adds white contours. Sample/face counts describe approximate coverage at the Band stage before other masks, spacing and cleanup. These overlays are not final plants or render output.

Manual retains the last completed result until Update scatter. Live updates relevant dependencies. A failed successor retains the previous complete result and reports the failure. If an Analyzer is stale, Analyze it first and then update Manual Scatter.

In Manual, enabled field feedback follows relevant authored/animated inputs while published plants and radii stay frozen. The label reads Pending field; plants from last Update. Field toggles, selection and XY/3D radius display do not solve placements. An uncached display mode cannot use changed source geometry alongside the preceding publication; Update is required.

Local identification-color edits retain unchanged sibling previews. Unchanged navigation reuses prepared display data. Heavy changed layers, cold loading and first panel construction can still take time.

Statistics identifies the selected layer and its last completed calculation. Requested and accepted placements are separate from prepared cloud points, centres or preview instances. Prepared samples are not current-frame draw counts. Marked for Update reports pending invalidation; Read cached statistics does not apply Manual edits. Empty successful results and failed updates have separate feedback. Optional diagnostics record local bounded events; recording is separate from sharing or permission to train.

In Viewport & render, Navigating and Idle set separate limits for Point Cloud points, Proxy instances or Mesh triangles across visible layers. Use 0 for unlimited. A short pause restores Idle detail; final rendering retains the full accepted planting. Expensive Mesh sources can use cached boxes to fit the triangle or memory allowance. Oversized Point Cloud requests use a bounded sample and report the memory reduction, including at zero limits; switching modes reuses the current planting snapshots. Zero removes artist draw caps but keeps memory safeguards. Graphics failure uses bounded centre markers. Display changes preserve pending Manual edits.

Open Viewport & render > Viewport memory… to choose Automatic or Custom 256–65,536 MiB. This preference is shared by Scatter controllers in this Max installation and is not saved in a scene or recipe. It controls future Mesh admission; it does not calculate planting, remove current resources or bypass Windows/device safeguards. After changing it, use Refresh display to retry published plants while keeping pending Manual placement edits pending. Raising it does not guarantee that every source fits.

From 0.82.6, saved reports include call counts, total time, longest time and failed-stage counts for input extraction, candidates, masks, transforms/radii, spacing, preview preparation, uploads, publication and panel work. Times are inclusive: a parent can contain another measured stage, so do not add all totals together. Action IDs connect an edit to invalidation and its deferred publication; unrelated host activity can have no action ID. The selected-setup snapshot reads cached requested/accepted/prepared counts and pending flags without evaluating the scene. These timings do not measure presented viewport FPS.

Edit instances#

Add Cyrus Scatter Edit, select Instances, then select and transform the instance handles. Unselected handles follow the existing Color by Model, Layer or Bands palette; selected handles keep their color with contrasting selection marks. Display, picking and the transform gizmo use the final displayed placement pivot. An offset source pivot is not automatically moved to the trunk.

During Move, the selected handle and gizmo follow the drag while full geometry presentation commits after release. The previous complete mesh can remain visible while its successor is prepared. This is not a promise of constant frame rate for every scene.

Removing a model keeps its move, deletion and clone history inactive. Compatible surviving candidate/source pairs retain their edits; a replacement model does not inherit another source’s history. Undo or re-adding the compatible original source can restore it. Changed generation, receiver geometry or incompatible source settings remain guarded.

Reset all edits clears the entire Edit modifier, not only the selected layer. It is explicit and Undoable. Preserve original scenes and save upgraded copies: plugins older than 0.86.9 cannot read the new source-aware Edit storage.

Whole-object Copy still has a limitation when an upper Edit references clones made by a lower Edit, or when radius overrides target clones. Those histories require coordinated ID remapping. Do not rely on that Copy case for duplication; preserve the original setup and validate a saved copy.

Final artist acceptance#

Get the 0.87.3 Windows EXE from the Download page, save work and close the selected Max versions. Select Max 2024, 2026 or 2027, then click Install/Update. Scatter and Surface Analyzer 0.14.2 install together; no separate Analyzer MZP is needed. Leave Install / update plant library unchecked to retain existing content. If you already have CyrusScatter-Content-0.86.7.zip, place it beside the EXE before checking that option. Reopen Max after completion; the unsigned installer does not launch or restart it.

The website provides one EXE containing both plugins. The optional plant content ZIP and standalone MZP downloads are excluded. Existing compatible content is reused and shared across standard Max profiles. Keep adopted folders available for saved scenes. Uninstall Scatter keeps the independent Analyzer, plant content and scenes.

Team-pilot builds expose License / activation. Export an activation request and import the returned license. The pilot license lasts 30 days from issuance; expiry locks authoring while existing scenes remain loadable/renderable.

Scatter 0.87.3 uses schema 61 and source-aware Edit storage 2. Schema-58 scenes require the explicit Undoable Upgrade scene action; save an upgraded copy. Earlier development schemas remain unsupported. This patch was runtime-tested only in Max 2027. The Max 2024/2026 payloads have native tests only; this 0.87.3 successor has not run inside those hosts. Earlier host and Corona-material results retain their original versions and scope. Library assets require compatible Corona and, where used, Forest plug-ins. Max 2025 support is not implied. Broad DPI/tablet, renderer and long production-session acceptance remain separate.

View the changelog for additions and fixes, or use the testing walkthrough to record your own observations.

Complete planting recipes#

Open Cyrus Library, or Layers > Recipes from the intended setup. Plant models > All models opens by default, with Trees, Shrubs, Flowers, Groundcover, Grasses, Leaves and Ground Details. There are 96 individual assets, covering the original 104 catalog cards after collection and duplicate cards are accounted for. Thumbnails use the prepared Corona renders and load as you scroll. Browsing, searching and selection do not calculate plants or modify the scene.

Merge model places the selected individual visibly in the scene; it does not require a selected terrain. Add to selected layer imports the model as a hidden source for the current Scatter layer while preserving the layer settings. Choose your receivers, mix sources and design the distribution yourself. In Manual mode, press Update scatter to apply placement changes. Missing material or map dependencies are reported; install compatible Corona/Forest plug-ins for the supplied assets. A visible banner confirms the added model and destination layer; failed imports show an error banner.

Personal My recipes and Custom library remain separate from individual models. Select the intended terrain and setup when loading a complete recipe; later scene selection does not redirect its captured destination. Save Recipe saves supported settings, optional preview and complete Paint. Include models, materials, terrain and paths is checked by default. Terrain is an evaluated geometry/channel snapshot. Saving pending Manual settings does not calculate plants. My recipes uses the shared registered local NTFS store; Manage storage shows its active folder.

Load onto surface imports independent supported models/materials and adds layers to the captured setup, creating one if needed. It preserves existing layers and Manual/Live mode, then updates once. One Undo removes the imported layers and assets; Redo restores them. If several setups share a terrain, open Recipes from the intended setup.

Complete presets convert physical sizes and distances into destination system units. Paint contours and static guide positions fit the saved local-XY footprint to the destination footprint. Brush radius, falloff, path widths and model dimensions remain physical. Terrain Paint presets transfer between single-valued local-XY footprints. Curved Paint presets require matching indexed topology; arbitrary remeshing does not preserve face correspondence. Settings-only exact Paint restoration keeps its compatible-receiver requirement.

Individual plant models are building blocks; a complete recipe stores an authored arrangement and supported bindings. Create your own mixed planting, then save and reuse it. The earlier eight procedural demonstration designs are historical deliveries and are no longer the default bundled library.

Update selected writes a new revision, Save Copy creates a new recipe identity, and Edit details changes presentation without touching the scene. Use Export library / collection and Import shared library to transfer verified assets and recipes. Settings-only recipes need supported assets saved before direct loading.

The static adapter supports standalone meshes, Standard/Blinn materials and static PNG maps. XRefs, arbitrary renderer shaders/proxies, animated dependencies and authored Scatter Edit/per-instance radius codecs remain outside this adapter. Missing or corrupt assets and capacity errors retain the existing planting.

Direction and normal blending#

In Transforms > Orientation, choose Random, World direction or Look at target. World direction aims along a nonzero XYZ vector. Look at target aims toward the world pivot of a picked object. Models use local +Z up and the Forward axis set in Models & Points. Local random rotations still apply; zero their ranges to check exact aim.

Align to normal and Normal % set preferred up: disabled or 0% uses world +Z; 100% uses the geometric face normal, with angular blending between. Direction modes use this to control roll while preserving heading. Slope eligibility is independent. Coincident targets and parallel heading/up use deterministic fallbacks.

Manual waits for Update. Live follows relevant target/parent or orientation animation. Missing targets and zero vectors retain the last complete plants and report failure. Editing the target shape or rotating it around an unchanged pivot does not calculate scatter.

Complete recipes bind orientation targets as external roles. Numeric Transform presets preserve the destination target and require it for Look at target. New complete recipes use format 8 and numeric settings presets use format 3. Grid distances convert with scene units; earlier complete formats receive neutral Surface random defaults. Complete recipe formats 1/2 retain original receiver random inputs when read; format 1 also receives neutral orientation defaults. Reading never rewrites Paint or files. Physical picker, 4K and mixed-monitor testing remains artist acceptance.

Copy and import variation#

Choose Same variation (default) or New variation before copying a layer. Both create independent layer ownership and Paint. Same retains receiver random inputs; New chooses fresh inputs once. Changing the choice is passive.

Recipes default to New variation. Choose Saved variation to retain the saved random inputs, then Add layers or Create new setup. Exact matching requires identical evaluated terrain, receiver history, quotas, source order/weights, masks, Relax and collision context. Complete presets transfer supported Paint across units and local-XY footprints; exact settings-only Paint retains compatible geometry/frame/unit requirements.

Amount settings presets separately offer Saved seed, Keep current seed or New seed. These numeric presets do not contain complete arrangements. Redo restores the chosen variation rather than rerolling.

Named layer Copy rejects authored Scatter Edit and per-instance radius data. Max object Copy retains the tested simple-stack workflow, but clone-dependent multiple-Edit stacks and clone-targeted radius overrides still need coordinated remapping. Preserve the original and verify any duplicate. Resource rejection retains the previous complete result; arbitrary low-memory conditions and sustained production-session acceptance remain separate.

Install or update Cyrus Scatter#

Download the 0.87.3 Windows EXE from the Download page. Save your work and close the selected Max versions before running it. Select Max 2024, 2026 or 2027, choose Install / Update, and reopen Max after completion. Scatter and Surface Analyzer 0.14.2 install together for each selected host.

The website supplies the installer only. Leave Install / update plant library unchecked for a plugin-only installation or to preserve an existing library. You can use your own scene objects without the optional plant library.

If you already have CyrusScatter-Content-0.86.7.zip, place it beside the EXE and check the library option. Existing verified content is reused in one shared store across standard profiles. The large content ZIP and separate MZPs are not included in this website download.

The installer is an unsigned user-test build. Library materials using Corona or Forest maps require matching plug-ins. Real Corona leaf-material qualification remains Max 2027; older-host material tests used Standard materials.

Drag rollout headers to arrange the Modify panel. Max retains the saved order when you reselect Scatter and packs whole rollouts into columns; a tall open section can leave a gap when it does not fit. The installer's Uninstall Scatter action keeps the independently installed Analyzer, shared content and scenes.

Plants that respond to nearby objects#

In a stone or tree layer, enable Interactions > Collider. In a grass or flower layer, choose each distinct source, click Analyze model, inspect its roots, branch directions and foliage attachments, then Accept reviewed guides and enable React to colliders. Prepare each source once; its instances reuse that definition with independent transforms and contact poses.

Apply interactions updates contact against the last completed scatter. Pending Manual amount and seed changes still wait for Update scatter. Use Cyrus Edit > Instances to move an individual collider and update nearby reacting plants.

Contact gap adds visible world-space clearance; zero still accounts for prepared stem thickness. Hide roots under colliders suppresses covered rooted groups and restores them when the obstacle moves. Preview leaves / blades selects a stable sample for display; full render and Bake keep all visible source faces.

This is static rooted contact. It does not provide wind animation, inertia, plant self-collision or two-way rigid dynamics. Guide inference requires review and supports specific geometric profiles; unresolved sources are rejected. Validate full visible mesh performs a slower independent triangle check.

Lightweight tree colliders#

Keep the detailed visual tree. Select its source and use Build trunk colliders to create a separate closed collision shape, then Review collider. Tree collider construction does not require plant stem analysis. The proxy follows each published instance through Cyrus Edit.

Automatic trunks approximate a connected lower trunk and need review. Exposed roots, irregular bases and curved trunks may need Pick closed collider mesh with a manually prepared, closed manifold shape. Automatic fitted-root generation is not available in this build. Author custom geometry relative to the original source, rather than an arbitrary scattered instance.

Minimum stem length is stored in metres and displayed in scene units, with a 1–100 mm range on the source before scatter scaling. Repair preparation settings converts valid legacy values or restores invalid values to 5 mm / 5%, without resizing scene geometry. Display-unit labels alone do not change physical size.

Shared models, recipes and textures#

Open Layers > Recipes for Cyrus Library. Save Recipe with Include models, materials, terrain and paths captures supported static assets. Library > Save selected scene models saves one to ten selected static models. Reuse them through My models, Merge model or Add to selected layer.

A managed local NTFS store shares identical mesh and image bytes across recipes and collections. Recipes pin saved revisions; changing a scene material does not modify saved library assets. Use Export library / collection and Import shared library to transfer a verified .cyruslib bundle. Repeating an unchanged import does not duplicate cards or payloads.

Use Library > Manage storage for the active location and explicit maintenance actions. Shared root paths are limited to 80 characters. Version 0.87.3 corrects the default settings-folder lookup and saving the chosen location.

Portable textures require normal default OCIO and matching colour/renderer profiles. Unsupported dependencies are rejected explicitly. Collider/React roles, reviewed plant preparation and custom collider links are not yet portable through recipes; keep their complete Max scenes. The installed Plant models import route retains a separate Undo-history limitation.

headings.title: Plants that respond to nearby objects

search.title: Start with a layer
search.text: Create a Cyrus Scatter controller, add a layer, assign its receiving surfaces and add models or Points. Set Amount, then press Update scatter in Manual mode. Live responds to relevant edits.

search.title: Start with a layer
search.text: Use Geometry > Cyrus > Cyrus Scatter to create a controller, then exit Create mode and select it in Modify. Each layer owns its surfaces, sources, amount, layout, transforms and spacing. Layer order matters when between-layer spacing is enabled.

search.title: Start with a layer
search.text: Use Add, Copy, Remove, Up and Down to organize layers. Copy includes independent Paint Areas. Visible controls viewport display; Enabled controls the layer contribution. Removing an assignment does not delete the source scene object.

search.title: Start with a layer
search.text: In 0.82.6, closed sections create controls on first opening and reuse them while the command panel remains mounted. Switching layers rebinds those controls. Browsing does not apply pending Manual edits.

search.title: Start with a layer
search.text: Schema 61 stores reviewed plant preparation, physical minimum distances and source-bound colliders. Schema-60 preparation needs explicit review or repair. Schema-59 scenes open with Interactions off. Schema-58 scenes require the explicit Undoable Upgrade scene action. Preserve original files and save upgraded copies.

search.title: Scene source access
search.text: In Models & Points, highlight source rows and expand Source access. Select sources selects their scene nodes. Show sources and Hide sources change node visibility in one Undo while preserving renderable flags, registration, materials and completed plants. Max layer/group/category visibility restrictions still apply.

search.title: Scene source access
search.text: For one model with an assigned material, Edit material opens that scene material in Slate. Shared instances change together. Point/Empty, mixed and missing-material selections are guarded; library asset files remain unchanged.

search.title: Surfaces, models and optional containers
search.text: Add receivers to the selected layer. Unchanged receivers retain their base random streams when another receiver is added, renamed or reordered. Density gives each receiver its own count below the cap; Fixed Total redistributes the same total, so some existing candidates may be removed. Geometry changes, Relax, masks and shared spacing can change accepted output.

search.title: Surfaces, models and optional containers
search.text: Use + below Models & Points to add a model. Add Point, beside Make point, creates markers without final model geometry. Pick object replaces one selected Point or existing model while preserving its row identity, label, weight, scale, radius, offset and Band assignments. Make point converts a model row to a Point; the original scene object is retained. Duplicate sources and receiver picks are rejected. Empty choices create weighted gaps in Candidate budget mode; Accepted target rejects positive-weight Empty rows.

search.title: Surfaces, models and optional containers
search.text: Source controls include label, identification color, weight, scale, Manual/Auto radius, vertical offset and forward axis. Manual preserves its radius and optional Follow Scale. Auto bounds supported geometry around the pivot after final instance scale and orientation; it is conservative spacing, not exact mesh collision. Points, Empty and unqualified source families remain Manual. Assignment-group colors are separate from identification colors.

search.title: Surfaces, models and optional containers
search.text: Source containers are optional palettes. New rectangles start with Enable collection off. Position and resize first, then enable collection to collect eligible source pivots. Selecting a rectangle opens compact collection and dimension controls; select the Scatter controller for full planting settings. Moving an enabled rectangle carries its owned models; resizing its boundary leaves their transforms unchanged. Disabling collection parks models while retaining settings. Manual waits for Update; Live applies relevant membership changes.

search.title: Surfaces, models and optional containers
search.text: Removing the last model clears its scattered output after Update in Manual, or automatically in Live. The empty layer remains valid when Amount changes. Adding a replacement restores planting. Point and intentional Empty gap rows retain their distinct behavior.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Planting positions chooses Surface random, Rectangular, Staggered or Hexagonal. Grids expose world-unit spacing, fixed Origin X/Y, Heading and stable Jitter. They project down onto the highest receiver hit. Hexagonal calculates row pitch from its nearest-neighbor distance. Count/Density and refill are inactive; masks and collision rules thin the lattice. Source assignment below is independent. Entirely vertical receivers and Analyzer Single/EdgeRow positions are unsupported with grids.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Random mix chooses weighted sources. Clusters choose assignment groups across space. Spline Bands use closed world-XY Paths, explicit Models / Points or Assignment groups, and Consecutive or Independent ranges. Surface Analyzer consumes separately analyzed boundary, path and point channels.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Consecutive accumulates widths separately on each Path/side and preserves unassigned intervals as gaps. Independent exposes each Band's Start/End and combines eligible contributions. New Bands start unassigned. Scaling a Path changes its outline, not its world-space Band distances.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Density and its optional curve shape a Band's contribution from Start to End. Independent contributions cap total occupancy at 100%, then choose the Band proportionally. A 100% Sphere plus 25% Box gives approximately 80% Sphere/20% Box in the overlap and 25% occupancy where only Box contributes, before other masks/spacing.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Rounded uses distance to original border segments. Sharp uses bounded miter offsets; acute corners have limits and narrow/complex requests can require simplification. The preview shows admitted geometry.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: Amount supports Count or area Density, up to 1,000,000 per population. A controller shares a 1,000,000-candidate work limit across its populations, including retry and protected-edit requirements. Exceeding that limit reports an error and retains the preceding result. Candidate budget can underfill after restrictions. Independent ranges and nontrivial Band density require Candidate budget; Accepted target is rejected so retries cannot erase the fade. Use a fixed seed for repeatable comparisons. Texture Density uses a selected UV channel (1..99, default 1) on each receiver. Choose 64, 128, 256 or 512 samples per side (default 128). Higher resolution helps capture narrow mask details at a greater preparation cost. UVs clamp to 0..1; white permits and black excludes. Unchanged maps reuse their sampled data across receiver edits. Errors identify the invalid receiver/channel and retain the previous complete result.

search.title: Layout and Amount
search.text: 0.86.0 keeps placement-sized calculation and storage in native memory. Count changes no longer reserve MAXScript heap proportional to every plant. Undo remains available; a failed successor preserves the last complete result. The one-million controller work limit and memory safeguards remain. Large calculations, complex source geometry and Bake can still block Max while they finish.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Image / pattern density and Surface density are independent. White permits plants, black excludes them and gray thins them. Their enabled fields multiply with Paint and terrain eligibility before spacing.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Choose pattern selects Uniform, Soft patches or Wide bands. Image selects a file. Both choose projected World XY. Physical tile size, rotation, offsets and Repeat/Clamp control the image footprint. Scatter local XY follows the setup frame; Receiver UV reads the explicitly selected UV channel.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Map selects Map coordinates and evaluates supported graphs against each receiver. Vertex Color reads its own numeric channel, and Checker reads its own UV channel. Color Correction and Output chains retain those inputs. Supported classes also include Bitmap, Mix, Noise, RGB Multiply and Gradient. A surface material is not a density map; renderer/camera-dependent graphs reject with a useful explanation.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Both Map targets accept a TextureMap dragged from the Material Editor, including when empty. Procedural maps show a small cached thumbnail. Drag the texture map itself rather than a complete material. Receiver-dependent graphs can look different on the surface; use Show mask to inspect their evaluated density.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Clear removes the map and disables image density. The independent surface field stays enabled if it was enabled. Disabling Use image alone preserves its map for later. Image or pattern selection restores projected coordinates; Map restores receiver-aware coordinates.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Enable Use surface density and choose Mesh channel to read stored numeric values from the evaluated receiver. Channel 0 reads vertex colors; channels 1..99 select numbered map data. Choose R/X, G/Y or B/Z, then Input min/max, Invert and the response curve. Every receiver must contain the requested channel. Data Channel or VertexPaint can author it; Scatter does not invent missing data.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Relative elevation uses evaluated local height: low is 0, high is 1 and flat terrain is 0. Node translation, rotation and scale preserve this field. It creates no mesh channel. Valley moss and Mountain planting use it so their library entries no longer depend on channel 2 or the original world altitude.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Show mask displays Image, Surface field or Combined density and follows relevant edits. Manual plants remain at the last Update while the preview can show current inputs. Live follows relevant map/channel edits and animation. Idle and unrelated animation do not evaluate maps or solve Scatter. A failed update retains the complete previous result.

search.title: Image, map and surface density
search.text: Native map sampling uses unfiltered scalar values. The map graph and receiver work are bounded; unsupported requirements and oversized inputs reject cleanly. Projected maps can use an explicit portable image snapshot. Receiver-aware graphs remain editable in Max scenes but cannot be exported as arbitrary procedural packages or baked into a context-free tile.

search.title: Band scale profiles
search.text: In Layout, Scale sits directly below the density curve. Min/Max supplies random size variation. Scale profile selects Off, Follow Density or Custom. Custom enables Edit scale curve. X runs from Band Start to End; Y is size percent, where 100% preserves size.

search.title: Band scale profiles
search.text: Density and scale have independent curves. Follow Density uses the effective density curve shape, without the Density % strength; disabling that density curve gives a flat 100% scale profile. Switching modes keeps the Custom graph. Zero size does not remove a candidate.

search.title: Band scale profiles
search.text: Scale curves multiply existing source, Band and layer size once. Auto Radius follows final size; Manual radius needs Follow Scale. Size-dependent spacing can change accepted counts. Manual requires Update scatter. Steep Sharp profiles can exceed the bounded precision and retain the previous result; simplify the curve or choose Rounded.

search.title: Slope and altitude filters
search.text: Enable Filter slope or Filter altitude in Include / exclude areas > Surface eligibility. Slope is measured from world up using the evaluated geometric normal: 0 degrees upward, 90 degrees vertical, 180 degrees downward. Altitude is world Z at the final receiver anchor, before source pivot offsets.

search.title: Slope and altitude filters
search.text: Lower and Upper fade soften density inside the range. For a 0-35 degree slope interval, a 10 degree upper fade thins between 25 and 35 degrees. Zero fade includes the endpoint. Fades cannot overlap; invalid settings retain the previous complete result.

search.title: Slope and altitude filters
search.text: Filters preserve surviving candidate IDs, model choices and transforms. Paint overlap still uses max-union density; explicitly moved or cloned CS Edit plants bypass these filters. Spacing and cleanup follow filtering. Use Candidate budget to retain the visible density fade; Accepted target can refill within its finite work budget.

search.title: Slope and altitude filters
search.text: Manual waits for Update; Live follows relevant edits and receiver animation. The status describes the last calculated prepared pool, separately from accepted plants. Heights use scene units and survive scene-unit conversion.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Use Presets... in Amount, Transforms or Spacing & cleanup. Curve presets are available from Paint, Analyzer and Band density/scale graphs. Save new captures a named item; selecting it is passive, and Apply changes the target shown in the dialog. Reopen the browser to target a different layer.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Population includes amount, density, seed and retry policy. Transforms include the layer rotation, scale, movement, normal alignment and projection. Assets, surfaces, IDs, maps and layout remain linked to the scene. Physical distances convert across system units; density stays per square metre.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Spacing stores the effective rule and applies an explicit override in the chosen Within this layer or Between layers scope. It does not store peer identities or change Relax/cleanup. Reset inheritance remains a separate control.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Curve presets preserve samples and editable handles while retaining enable flags, widths and scale ranges. Density and Paint scale use zero-to-one values; other scale curves support multipliers. Invalid or incompatible curves are rejected. One Undo/Redo restores Apply, and closing a graph after Undo does not reapply the preset.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: Manual waits for Update scatter; Live follows normal update callbacks. Browsing, saving and renaming do not calculate plants. Animated or expression-controlled targets are rejected. Static shared controllers are detached so another owner is preserved.

search.title: Named settings and curve presets
search.text: The local library is CyrusScatter/Presets inside the per-user Max PlugCFG directory. Share the .cspreset.json files. Limits are 512 files, 64 KiB per file and 80-character names. Rename changes the library name; Delete confirms removal of the selected file. Invalid files and failed writes report errors. Complete static recipes and explicit role substitution are available through Layers > Recipes.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Turn on Use Paint Areas, add a named area and choose one receiver from the layer. Select Paint or Erase, set Radius and press Start Brush. Paint joins circular footprints into a vector region; Erase cuts coverage and holes. Stop ends the session.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Areas share the layer models and population. Overlap contributes coverage once per candidate. Turning Paint Areas off retains the areas and uses the full receiver. Fill and Clear operate on the selected area; keep a saved copy before major edits.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Inward/outward feather widths and separate density/scale curves shape the edge. Density changes acceptance; scale multiplies model size. A 100 mm radius has a 200 mm diameter. Borders describe coverage, not guaranteed accepted plants.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Hover over Paint controls for short descriptions. Fade density changes plant acceptance; Fade scale changes size independently. Inside and Outside fade define the transition width. With the default curve, Edge scale is the outer-end size multiplier and Inner scale is the interior multiplier: 0.5 means half size, 1 unchanged and 2 double. Edge scale cannot exceed Inner scale. The graph shapes the transition between them.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Vector painting supports terrain, spheres, boxes, vertical sides and manifold curved meshes. Curved strokes follow surface distance across connected edges without painting through to the opposite side or disconnected sheets. Degenerate faces and nonmanifold connections require repair.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: The vector format introduced in 0.78 does not convert earlier stroke setups. Preserve older scenes with their matching build and create a new setup for the vector workflow.

search.title: Vector painting
search.text: Curved Paint retains Paint/Erase, Fill/Clear, independent density and scale fade curves, Undo/Redo and saved scenes. Curved mesh distance includes nonuniform receiver scaling. Surface coverage uses vector face regions with bounded work: up to 100,000 triangles and 200,000 vertices, with separate contour and solver limits. Terrain keeps its existing projected vector behavior.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Stop the brush and select a Paint Area. Export spline offers Optimized and Exact snapshot. Optimized reduces planar knots within a world-unit maximum deviation, initially 1 mm, and reports the reduction; attached-surface boundaries default to Exact. Cases that cannot be certified retain Exact geometry with a reason. Export leaves original Paint and completed plants unchanged. Reopen the options if the captured owner, area or receiver changes. Edit the exported spline, then choose Replace or Add and Pick spline... to import it explicitly.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: For terrain, export uses the receiver's local XY plane at local Z=0 with its scene transform. On terrain the spline is a planar editing guide. Import projects along receiver-local Z, clips to the receiver and requires every contour to be closed. Nested loops and self-intersections use even-odd fill regardless of winding or order.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Replace sets coverage; Add unions it with the existing region without erasing paint. Density, fades, models and area identity stay unchanged. A changed import and each export are one Undo. Manual waits for Update; Live follows changed coverage. There is no live source link: later spline edits require another import.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Curve tolerance is a world-unit approximation distance, initially 1 mm. Smaller values need more samples. An edited shape is limited to 8,192 input knots and 8,192 sampled vertices; unchanged guarded surface snapshots use the canonical contour budget. Paint precision imposes a minimum tolerance; very large local coordinates can prevent accurate Max spline export. Invalid conversion retains existing paint. Reopen using the saved scene units; native Paint geometry conversion guards still apply.

search.title: Paint and spline snapshots
search.text: Curved receivers export a 3D surface border. An unchanged exported snapshot restores exact coverage, including holes and large regions. Edited closed curves must lie on the receiver within Curve tolerance and select the smaller enclosed region on a closed component. A fully filled closed object has no border to export. The generic 8,192-knot import limit applies to edited curves; exact guarded snapshots use the native contour limit.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Closed Include shapes union their eligible domains. Exclude takes precedence. Area masks test placement support rather than trimming model geometry. Layout & soft boundaries explains guide widths and edge curves.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Rotation, XYZ scale, whole scale and movement have independent ranges and reset buttons. Projection and orientation settings affect final placement.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: In Models & Points > Radius and clearance, give each selected model its radius and independently choose Own copies, Other models in this layer and Other layers. Each scope can use layer defaults or its own supported request. Other-layer requests can target selected layers or all other layers in this setup.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: For an explicit model request, clearance is factor × (radius A + radius B) + gap, measured in XY or full 3D. Protected edits reserve space first, then eligible preferred models, then layer and stable candidate order. Prefer this model resolves conflicts after Count admission; it does not take extra Count slots. These are pivot-radius tests rather than exact mesh collisions.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Use Spacing & cleanup for layer defaults and candidate Relax. Point Relax and Boundary Relax are visible above Advanced. Enabling a mode reveals its controls. The shared Relax distance means desired separation for Point Relax or neighbor-search radius for Boundary Relax; it stays editable when either is enabled. Boundary Relax smooths candidates within its movement cap. Clearance filters the moved candidates afterward.

search.title: Area limits, transforms and spacing
search.text: Advanced retains layer-owned selected-instance radius overrides and accepted cleanup. Cyrus Scatter Edit > Instances adjusts published instances using stable candidate/source identities. Generation and receiver changes can invalidate bindings; a blocked edit retains its saved history. Radius overlays are inspection aids. In Manual mode, press Update scatter to apply placement edits.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Placement points shows one marker per accepted placement. Point Cloud, Proxy and Mesh have separate display budgets, so shown counts can be lower than accepted output. Choose Textured mesh in Display mode for supported source base colors, UV channels and cutout opacity. Color by offers Layer, Model and Bands identification colors for nontextured modes. Use Surfaces > Hide surface to hide receiver drawing while keeping painting and rendering. The choice is shared by setups using that node and supports Undo and scene saving.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Textured Mesh covers Standard and Corona Legacy/Physical base color and opacity, Multi/Sub face IDs and supported Bitmap, Checker and Color Correction map chains. Each color or opacity branch requires one common explicit UV channel; the branches may differ. The two-sided preview uses bounded 256-pixel tiles and an alpha cutoff, rather than full Corona shading, translucency or blended transparency. Forest Color omits per-instance Forest variation. Unsupported branches report fallback; missing UV channels retain the preceding complete display. Source render materials are preserved.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Supported material, UV and color-management edits refresh appearance without changing placement publication or applying pending Manual edits. Colored Mesh preserves supported leaf cutouts while showing identification colors. Radius-only updates reuse compatible source geometry, UVs and material data. Source geometry changes still require Update before the new appearance can be paired with the plants; shared animated maps follow relevant forward and reverse time changes.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Color by Bands follows the accepted owner even when Bands share a model. Preview Falloff shows selected contribution or Combined density on receiver surfaces: blue is zero and red is 100%. Show Boundaries adds white contours. Sample/face counts describe approximate coverage at the Band stage before other masks, spacing and cleanup. These overlays are not final plants or render output.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Manual retains the last completed result until Update scatter. Live updates relevant dependencies. A failed successor retains the previous complete result and reports the failure. If an Analyzer is stale, Analyze it first and then update Manual Scatter.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: In Manual, enabled field feedback follows relevant authored/animated inputs while published plants and radii stay frozen. The label reads Pending field; plants from last Update. Field toggles, selection and XY/3D radius display do not solve placements. An uncached display mode cannot use changed source geometry alongside the preceding publication; Update is required.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Local identification-color edits retain unchanged sibling previews. Unchanged navigation reuses prepared display data. Heavy changed layers, cold loading and first panel construction can still take time.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Statistics identifies the selected layer and its last completed calculation. Requested and accepted placements are separate from prepared cloud points, centres or preview instances. Prepared samples are not current-frame draw counts. Marked for Update reports pending invalidation; Read cached statistics does not apply Manual edits. Empty successful results and failed updates have separate feedback. Optional diagnostics record local bounded events; recording is separate from sharing or permission to train.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: In Viewport & render, Navigating and Idle set separate limits for Point Cloud points, Proxy instances or Mesh triangles across visible layers. Use 0 for unlimited. A short pause restores Idle detail; final rendering retains the full accepted planting. Expensive Mesh sources can use cached boxes to fit the triangle or memory allowance. Oversized Point Cloud requests use a bounded sample and report the memory reduction, including at zero limits; switching modes reuses the current planting snapshots. Zero removes artist draw caps but keeps memory safeguards. Graphics failure uses bounded centre markers. Display changes preserve pending Manual edits.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: Open Viewport & render > Viewport memory… to choose Automatic or Custom 256–65,536 MiB. This preference is shared by Scatter controllers in this Max installation and is not saved in a scene or recipe. It controls future Mesh admission; it does not calculate planting, remove current resources or bypass Windows/device safeguards. After changing it, use Refresh display to retry published plants while keeping pending Manual placement edits pending. Raising it does not guarantee that every source fits.

search.title: Preview, updates, output and diagnostics
search.text: From 0.82.6, saved reports include call counts, total time, longest time and failed-stage counts for input extraction, candidates, masks, transforms/radii, spacing, preview preparation, uploads, publication and panel work. Times are inclusive: a parent can contain another measured stage, so do not add all totals together. Action IDs connect an edit to invalidation and its deferred publication; unrelated host activity can have no action ID. The selected-setup snapshot reads cached requested/accepted/prepared counts and pending flags without evaluating the scene. These timings do not measure presented viewport FPS.

search.title: Edit instances
search.text: Add Cyrus Scatter Edit, select Instances, then select and transform the instance handles. Unselected handles follow the existing Color by Model, Layer or Bands palette; selected handles keep their color with contrasting selection marks. Display, picking and the transform gizmo use the final displayed placement pivot. An offset source pivot is not automatically moved to the trunk.

search.title: Edit instances
search.text: During Move, the selected handle and gizmo follow the drag while full geometry presentation commits after release. The previous complete mesh can remain visible while its successor is prepared. This is not a promise of constant frame rate for every scene.

search.title: Edit instances
search.text: Removing a model keeps its move, deletion and clone history inactive. Compatible surviving candidate/source pairs retain their edits; a replacement model does not inherit another source’s history. Undo or re-adding the compatible original source can restore it. Changed generation, receiver geometry or incompatible source settings remain guarded.

search.title: Edit instances
search.text: Reset all edits clears the entire Edit modifier, not only the selected layer. It is explicit and Undoable. Preserve original scenes and save upgraded copies: plugins older than 0.86.9 cannot read the new source-aware Edit storage.

search.title: Edit instances
search.text: Whole-object Copy still has a limitation when an upper Edit references clones made by a lower Edit, or when radius overrides target clones. Those histories require coordinated ID remapping. Do not rely on that Copy case for duplication; preserve the original setup and validate a saved copy.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Get the 0.87.3 Windows EXE from the Download page, save work and close the selected Max versions. Select Max 2024, 2026 or 2027, then click Install/Update. Scatter and Surface Analyzer 0.14.2 install together; no separate Analyzer MZP is needed. Leave Install / update plant library unchecked to retain existing content. If you already have CyrusScatter-Content-0.86.7.zip, place it beside the EXE before checking that option. Reopen Max after completion; the unsigned installer does not launch or restart it.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: The website provides one EXE containing both plugins. The optional plant content ZIP and standalone MZP downloads are excluded. Existing compatible content is reused and shared across standard Max profiles. Keep adopted folders available for saved scenes. Uninstall Scatter keeps the independent Analyzer, plant content and scenes.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Team-pilot builds expose License / activation. Export an activation request and import the returned license. The pilot license lasts 30 days from issuance; expiry locks authoring while existing scenes remain loadable/renderable.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: Scatter 0.87.3 uses schema 61 and source-aware Edit storage 2. Schema-58 scenes require the explicit Undoable Upgrade scene action; save an upgraded copy. Earlier development schemas remain unsupported. This patch was runtime-tested only in Max 2027. The Max 2024/2026 payloads have native tests only; this 0.87.3 successor has not run inside those hosts. Earlier host and Corona-material results retain their original versions and scope. Library assets require compatible Corona and, where used, Forest plug-ins. Max 2025 support is not implied. Broad DPI/tablet, renderer and long production-session acceptance remain separate.

search.title: Final artist acceptance
search.text: View the changelog for additions and fixes, or use the testing walkthrough to record your own observations.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Open Cyrus Library, or Layers > Recipes from the intended setup. Plant models > All models opens by default, with Trees, Shrubs, Flowers, Groundcover, Grasses, Leaves and Ground Details. There are 96 individual assets, covering the original 104 catalog cards after collection and duplicate cards are accounted for. Thumbnails use the prepared Corona renders and load as you scroll. Browsing, searching and selection do not calculate plants or modify the scene.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Merge model places the selected individual visibly in the scene; it does not require a selected terrain. Add to selected layer imports the model as a hidden source for the current Scatter layer while preserving the layer settings. Choose your receivers, mix sources and design the distribution yourself. In Manual mode, press Update scatter to apply placement changes. Missing material or map dependencies are reported; install compatible Corona/Forest plug-ins for the supplied assets. A visible banner confirms the added model and destination layer; failed imports show an error banner.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Personal My recipes and Custom library remain separate from individual models. Select the intended terrain and setup when loading a complete recipe; later scene selection does not redirect its captured destination. Save Recipe saves supported settings, optional preview and complete Paint. Include models, materials, terrain and paths is checked by default. Terrain is an evaluated geometry/channel snapshot. Saving pending Manual settings does not calculate plants. My recipes uses the shared registered local NTFS store; Manage storage shows its active folder.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Load onto surface imports independent supported models/materials and adds layers to the captured setup, creating one if needed. It preserves existing layers and Manual/Live mode, then updates once. One Undo removes the imported layers and assets; Redo restores them. If several setups share a terrain, open Recipes from the intended setup.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Complete presets convert physical sizes and distances into destination system units. Paint contours and static guide positions fit the saved local-XY footprint to the destination footprint. Brush radius, falloff, path widths and model dimensions remain physical. Terrain Paint presets transfer between single-valued local-XY footprints. Curved Paint presets require matching indexed topology; arbitrary remeshing does not preserve face correspondence. Settings-only exact Paint restoration keeps its compatible-receiver requirement.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Individual plant models are building blocks; a complete recipe stores an authored arrangement and supported bindings. Create your own mixed planting, then save and reuse it. The earlier eight procedural demonstration designs are historical deliveries and are no longer the default bundled library.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: Update selected writes a new revision, Save Copy creates a new recipe identity, and Edit details changes presentation without touching the scene. Use Export library / collection and Import shared library to transfer verified assets and recipes. Settings-only recipes need supported assets saved before direct loading.

search.title: Complete planting recipes
search.text: The static adapter supports standalone meshes, Standard/Blinn materials and static PNG maps. XRefs, arbitrary renderer shaders/proxies, animated dependencies and authored Scatter Edit/per-instance radius codecs remain outside this adapter. Missing or corrupt assets and capacity errors retain the existing planting.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: In Transforms > Orientation, choose Random, World direction or Look at target. World direction aims along a nonzero XYZ vector. Look at target aims toward the world pivot of a picked object. Models use local +Z up and the Forward axis set in Models & Points. Local random rotations still apply; zero their ranges to check exact aim.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Align to normal and Normal % set preferred up: disabled or 0% uses world +Z; 100% uses the geometric face normal, with angular blending between. Direction modes use this to control roll while preserving heading. Slope eligibility is independent. Coincident targets and parallel heading/up use deterministic fallbacks.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Manual waits for Update. Live follows relevant target/parent or orientation animation. Missing targets and zero vectors retain the last complete plants and report failure. Editing the target shape or rotating it around an unchanged pivot does not calculate scatter.

search.title: Direction and normal blending
search.text: Complete recipes bind orientation targets as external roles. Numeric Transform presets preserve the destination target and require it for Look at target. New complete recipes use format 8 and numeric settings presets use format 3. Grid distances convert with scene units; earlier complete formats receive neutral Surface random defaults.
